target_customer: Data and analytics engineering teams, including analysts at growth teams of fintech companies, who write SQL
problem: Analysts depend on data engineers to build and test SQL models; Quary brings the model, test and deploy workflow into the browser so analysts can self-serve.
business_model: Open source core with a hosted browser SaaS platform

founders.name: Benjamin King
previous_startups: Tumelo (co-founder; led engineering through its Series A per YC launch post)
founders.background_notes: Source: YC company page and launch post; YC page also describes him as a former physicist.

founders.name: Louis Jordan
prior_employers: Amazon (software engineer in finance, four years)
founders.background_notes: Source: YC company page and launch post.

technical_complexity.rationale: A Rust data transformation engine that runs in the browser against Snowflake, BigQuery and DuckDB is non trivial, but the product reimplements known workflows.

defensibility.rationale: The core engine is open source, so copying was easy; Tobiko valued the Rust speed and compile times.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Tobiko Data bought the company and team on 2025-01-15 and cited Rust speed gains; no source says incumbents copied it first.

market_need_then: The founder says the idea came from friction scaling the data function at Tumelo; the first customer was a fast-growing fintech. No wider demand data was found.

branding.community_and_virality: Open source repo on GitHub (quarylabs/quary) with a Made by Quary badge; a company blog says the team wants to build an open source company.

brand_strength.rationale: Open source repo gave some developer visibility, but no press on the brand or name origin was found.

outcome_analysis: Quary built an open source Rust engine and browser analytics platform and joined YC in Winter 2024. Tobiko Data announced it acquired Quary on 2025-01-15, with the team joining Tobiko and Ben King working on SQLGlot performance. No price or terms were disclosed. The YC directory shows Inactive, consistent with the product being absorbed. The deal rewarded the technical engine rather than a large revenue story, but no sources give customer numbers.
notes: Company site returned HTTP 503. Round rests on VCBacked alone and the date conflicts with a 2024 founding year on welcome.ai (YC says 2023). No dated competitor source was found: the launch post names none, and searches returned undated pages, so the list is empty. Education not found. Directory status Inactive reconciles with the acquisition.
